title: The 50/30/20 Budgeting Guideline
text: The 50/30/20 budget framework divides take-home net income into roughly 50% for essential needs (rent, groceries, utilities, minimum debt payments), 30% for discretionary wants (dining out, entertainment), and 20% for savings, investments, and emergency reserves.
source_name: Reserve Bank of India Financial Education

title: Emergency Fund Sizing and Liquidity
text: An emergency fund should ideally cover 3 to 6 months of essential living expenses. It should be kept in highly liquid and safe instruments—such as high-yield savings accounts or liquid mutual funds—rather than locked into illiquid or volatile assets.

title: Compound Interest and the Rule of 72
text: Compound interest generates returns on both the initial principal and previously accumulated interest over time. The 'Rule of 72' is a simple mental calculation: divide 72 by the annual interest rate to estimate approximately how many years it takes for an investment to double (e.g., at 12% annual return, money doubles in roughly 72 / 12 = 6 years).

title: Systematic Investment Plans (SIP) and Rupee-Cost Averaging
text: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) allows individuals to invest a fixed amount periodically (usually monthly) into mutual funds. This enforces financial discipline and practices rupee-cost averaging: buying more units when market prices are low and fewer units when prices are high, smoothing out market volatility over long horizons.
source_name: Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) / SEBI

title: Index Funds and Market Diversification
text: Index funds are passively managed mutual funds that replicate an underlying stock index like the Nifty 50 or BSE Sensex. They offer broad diversification across major companies at significantly lower expense ratios compared to actively managed funds, reducing individual stock risk.

title: Credit Scores and CIBIL Ranges in India
text: In India, credit scores generated by bureaus (such as CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF High Mark) range from 300 to 900. A score of 750 and above is generally considered favorable by banks and NBFCs, improving approval chances and qualifying borrowers for lower loan interest rates.
source_name: Reserve Bank of India (Credit Information Regulations)

title: Credit Card Revolving Debt and Interest Traps
text: Paying only the 'Minimum Amount Due' on a credit card triggers revolving interest charges (often 36% to 42% annualized / 3% to 3.5% per month) on the entire outstanding balance and revokes the interest-free grace period on subsequent transactions. Paying the 'Total Amount Due' in full before the due date avoids all finance charges.
source_name: RBI Master Direction on Credit Card Operations

title: Loan EMI Structure and Amortization
text: Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) consists of two components: interest and principal repayment. In the early stages of a loan, a major portion of each EMI goes toward paying interest, while the principal balance amortizes slowly. Prepaying the principal early significantly reduces total borrowing cost over the life of the loan.
source_name: RBI Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders

title: Debt Repayment Strategies: Avalanche vs. Snowball
text: The Debt Avalanche method prioritizes paying off debts with the highest interest rate first while paying minimums on others, saving the maximum amount of money in total interest. The Debt Snowball method prioritizes paying the smallest loan balance first, generating quick psychological wins and momentum.

title: Public Provident Fund (PPF) Scheme
text: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is an Indian government-backed long-term savings scheme with a 15-year maturity period. PPF enjoys 'Exempt-Exempt-Exempt' (EEE) tax status, meaning the investment, accrued interest, and maturity amount are all exempt from income tax in India.
source_name: National Savings Institute / Ministry of Finance India

title: DICGC Bank Deposit Insurance Cover
text: In India, each depositor in an insured commercial or cooperative bank is insured up to a maximum of ₹5,00,000 (Rupees Five Lakh) for both principal and interest by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.
source_name: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC / RBI)

title: Digital Payment and UPI Safety: 'UPI PIN is Only for Sending Money'
text: Under RBI Kehta Hai consumer protection guidelines, entering your UPI PIN, scanning a QR code, or clicking an approval link ALWAYS deducts money from your account. Receiving money via UPI or Google Pay / PhonePe never requires entering your PIN. Never share OTPs, PINs, or password details.
source_name: RBI Kehta Hai / National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

title: Warning on Guaranteed High-Return Offers and Ponzi Schemes
text: Under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act), offering guaranteed high returns (such as 'double your money in a few months' or '20%+ guaranteed monthly profit') without regulatory authorization is illegal in India. Market investments naturally carry risk, and any scheme claiming high risk-free returns is a classic hallmark of financial fraud.

title: Term Life Insurance vs. Investment-Linked Policies
text: Pure term life insurance provides high financial protection coverage (sum assured) for beneficiaries at an affordable annual premium, with zero survival benefit. Mixing insurance with investment (such as traditional endowment or ULIP products) typically yields high commissions and suboptimal returns compared to buying term insurance and investing the difference in low-cost index funds.

title: Indian Income Tax Regimes Overview (Section 115BAC)
text: India offers two personal income tax regimes: the default New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), which features lower slab rates and a full tax rebate under Section 87A for taxable income up to ₹7,00,000 (resulting in zero tax liability for income up to ₹7 lakh), but disallows most deductions like 80C, 80D, and HRA; and the Old Tax Regime, which has higher slab rates but permits eligible deductions and exemptions. Taxpayers should compare total tax liability under both regimes based on their actual deductions before filing.

title: Inflation and Purchasing Power
text: Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money over time. If the annual inflation rate is 6% and savings earn only 4% in a standard bank account, the real rate of return is negative (-2%), meaning the money will buy fewer goods in the future. Long-term wealth preservation requires investments whose expected returns outpace inflation.
source_name: Reserve Bank of India Monetary Policy Education

title: Transparent Group Expense Splitting
text: Recording group expenses promptly and agreeing upon clear splitting methods (equal shares, exact rupee contributions, or itemized percentages) prevents resentment and unrecorded liabilities among roommates and friends. Prompt settlements maintain trust and financial transparency.

title: Fixed Deposits (FD) vs. Mutual Funds
text: Fixed Deposits (FDs) offer guaranteed interest rates and capital safety backed by DICGC insurance up to ₹5,00,000 per depositor. In contrast, mutual funds invest in market instruments (equities or debt), offering potential for inflation-beating returns without guaranteed capital protection, subject to market risk and investment horizons.
source_name: SEBI Investor Education / RBI Financial Education
